paper.title: Multi-Agent Combinatorial-Multi-Armed-Bandit framework for the Submodular Welfare Problem under Bandit Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-agent combinatorial bandit (MA-CMAB) for the Submodular Welfare Problem under full-bandit feedback
unmapped: Actions are partitions (partition matroid over agent-item pairs X = P x Q) assigning N items among M agents, with optional per-agent quotas
Welfare objective f(S) = sum_i w_i(s_i) with each w_i monotone submodular; only aggregate reward observed
The learner knows the number of agents M and items N and has access to an (alpha, delta, eta)-resilient offline algorithm (continuous greedy)
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, a learning policy selects a feasible allocation $A_t \in \mathcal{D}$, and receives a stochastic full-bandit reward: $r_t = f_t(A_t),\quad\text{where } f_t(A_t) \in [0,1] \text{ and } \mathbb{E}[f_t(A_t)] = f(A_t).$ ... only the aggregate reward $f_t(A_t)$ is observed after each round— no agent or item level feedback is available.

algorithms.name: Submodular welfare MA-CMAB Algorithm (explore-then-commit with resilient continuous greedy)

symbols.delta_res: resilience parameter of the offline algorithm; delta = 4MN+2M for continuous greedy
symbols.eta_res: number of oracle calls / explored actions; eta = (MN)^8 for continuous greedy
symbols.C_agg: aggregation constant (C = M if score aggregates M agentwise terms, else 1)

conditions: rewards f_t(A) in [0,1], i.i.d. across rounds
agent valuations monotone submodular with w_i(emptyset)=0
alpha = 1 - 1/e benchmark (continuous greedy resilient with epsilon <= 1/(MN)^2)
polynomial horizon T and polynomially bounded eta (to absorb additive 2*eta term)
results.notes: Alpha-regret with alpha = 1-1/e: alpha*T*f(OPT) - E[sum f_t(A_t)]. With continuous greedy (Theorem 4.2), delta=4MN+2M, eta=(MN)^8, C=M (Table 1). Proof leaves an additive 2*eta term absorbed under assumptions on T. Also restated as Theorem G.1. Corollary 6.8 gives the same rate conditional on the clean event.

symbols.delta_res: resilience parameter of the offline algorithm
symbols.m_explore: number of plays per explored action

conditions: conditional on the clean event E

source.label: thm:conditional
source.quote: With \(\mathrm{rad}\) as in \eqref{eq:rad}, the conditional expected regret satisfies \E[\mathcal{R}(T)\mid \mathcal{E}]\ \le\ \eta m + T\,\delta\,C\,\sqrt{\frac{\log T}{2m}}.

results.notes: Bound on expected alpha-regret conditioned on the clean event (P(E) >= 1 - 2 eta/T); quantity set to other because it is conditional. Restated as Theorem E.1.
